messages:
ashley: Heads-up — noticed a customer in EU got routed to a US model variant repeatedly over the last 20m. latency was fine but cost + cache miss exploded. anyone else seeing this?
jon: yep saw spikes in egress to us-east for tenant: acme-eu. telemetry shows fallback decisions firing a lot.
kevin: behavior came after yesterday's rollout of the cheap-variant preference policy, right? we deprioritized region affinity if cost delta > 30%.
dana: correct. policy was: prefer local unless cost delta > 0.3 and latency delta < 30ms. guessing host selection math mis-estimated latency delta.
ryan: logs show routing eval path: route->tier_check->quota_gate->variant_pref->route_exec. quota_gate passed, variant_pref picked us-west-1-quantized. here's the log sample:
```
[13:12:48] route_eval tenant=acme-eu region=eu-west-1 tier=enterprise delta_cost=0.35 delta_latency_est=12ms chosen_variant=us-west-1-q4 fallback_reason=cost_savings
```
marie: oh — delta_latency_est is from stale histograms (TTL 10m). if traffic pattern changed, estimate was stale. we need fresher latency sampling or prefer p50 over stale p90.
ashley: consequence: KV cache cold start across region, thrash on prefix cache, plus quota accounting skew. requests retried and triggered fallback loop to cheaper variants.
jon: observed retries because some model variants returned 503 then route policy retried to another region, then policy saw increased failures and flipped back, creating a bounce loop.
kevin: we should add a simple circuit-breaker on cross-region fallback: if cross-region egress for a tenant increases > X in Y, stop cost-based fallback for Z minutes and lock to local.
dana: agreed. also add a tight cooldown on variant re-selection to avoid flipflop.
ryan: on telemetry side: add a metric for "fallback_count_by_tenant_region" and emit a 1s-sampled spike when route selection changes region. will add dashboards.
marie: rollout UX note: console showed the new policy as an unscoped global flag. that made it easy to accidentally affect EU-enterprise tenants. Could we add scope granularity in the UI? per-region/per-tier toggle?
ashley: yes, we should default new routing policies to opt-in via canary groups, not global. revert is painful otherwise.
jon: quick mitigation I'll push now: revert cheap-variant-preference to previous threshold and enable the circuit-breaker patch in route evaluator.
prod-bot: deploy started by jon (canary: 5%). CI checks passed.
kevin: code change for circuit breaker (pseudo):
```
if cross_region_egress_rate(tenant) > 0.05 * req_rate and cross_region_egress_window < 10m:
  lock_variant_to_local(tenant, ttl=15m)
else:
  proceed_with_selection()
```
dana: also adding TTL bump on latency histograms to 30s and using p50 for recent decisions. low-risk and will reduce stale estimates.
ryan: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert: "tenant_cross_region_fallback_rate > 0.02 for 2m" -> paging to eng-platform on-call.
marie: UX follow-up: I'll open a tiny RFC for per-scope policy toggles and a console change to show affected tenants before applying global policy.
ashley: thanks — immediate action items: jon revert + circuit-breaker, dana bump histogram TTL, ryan dashboards/alert, marie RFC. postmortem if this hits > 5% of requests for > 30m.
jon: pushing canary now, will update in thread.
prod-bot: deploy canary succeeded (5%).
jon: canary looks stable for 10m, rollback not needed so far. still monitoring cold cache churn.
ashley: good work. please keep sampling traces for impacted tenant and attach a perf sample to the RFC.
